matters.title: Joint resolution authorizing a contract with Wesco Distribution, Inc., of Woodridge, Illinois, in the amount of $72,934 for Variable Frequency Drive (VFDs) Replacement and installation Services for Lake County Public Works Vernon Hills West Pump Station.
matters.text:
..Title
Joint resolution authorizing a contract with Wesco Distribution, Inc., of Woodridge, Illinois, in the amount of $72,934 for Variable Frequency Drive (VFDs) Replacement and installation Services for Lake County Public Works Vernon Hills West Pump Station.

..Staff Summary
* There is a need to replace six Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) that have reached the end of their operational life.
* The project will include removal of existing drives, installation, startup and associated electrical work.
* Public Works identified a cooperative purchasing contract with Wesco Distribution, Inc., Woodridge, Illinois, through Sourcewell Cooperative Agreement Contract 091422WES to procure equipment, products, or services.  The current term of the contract is through November 8, 2026.
* Pursuant to Article 33.115 Cooperative Joint Purchasing of the Lake County Purchasing Ordinance, Lake County may participate in a cooperative purchasing agreement with Wesco Distribution, Inc.
* This resolution authorizes and directs the County Purchasing agent to execute a contract with Wesco Distribution, Inc., Woodridge, Illinois, in the amount of $72,934 for the Variable Frequency Drive Replacement and installation Services.

..Body
RESOLUTION

WHEREAS, there is a need to replace six variable frequency drives that have reached the end of their operational life and secure installation services; and 

WHEREAS, Public Works identified a cooperative purchasing contract with Wesco Distribution, Inc, Woodridge, Illinois, through Sourcewell Cooperative Agreement Contract No. 091422WES to procure equipment, products, or services; and

WHEREAS, in accordance with Article 33.115 Cooperative Joint Purchasing of the Lake County Purchasing Ordinance, Lake County may participate in a cooperative purchasing agreement for the procurement of goods and services in accordance with an agreement entered between the participants; and

WHEREAS, the current term of the Sourcewell contract expires on November 8, 2026.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by this County Board of Lake County, Illinois, that the Purchasing Agent is hereby authorized and directed to execute the attached contract with Wesco Distribution, Inc, Woodridge, Illinois, in the amount of $72,934 for the variable frequency drive (VFD) replacement and installation services.

DATED at Waukegan, Illinois, on November 12, 2024.

matters.title: Joint resolution accepting a grant from Congressionally Directed Spending through the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) Community Grants Projects to support the Lake County New Century Town Water Reclamation Facility (NCT WRF) Centrifuge Project, including an emergency appropriation of $959,752 in grant funds and an emergency appropriation from Fund 610 Public Works Fund reserves.
matters.text:
..Title
Joint resolution accepting a grant from Congressionally Directed Spending through the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) Community Grants Projects to support the Lake County New Century Town Water Reclamation Facility (NCT WRF) Centrifuge Project, including an emergency appropriation of $959,752 in grant funds and an emergency appropriation from Fund 610 Public Works Fund reserves.

..Staff Summary
* Lake County Department of Public Works (LCPW) owns and operates the NCT WRF in Vernon Hills. The NCT WRF is the second largest of the three LCPW treatment plants.
* All WRFs require a dewatering process to separate the solid waste from clear effluent. The current dewatering equipment at NCT WRF is in need of replacement. 
* The NCT WRF Project will replace the existing belt filter presses and associated equipment in the sludge dewatering building with new centrifuge technology. 
* The grant amount totaling $959,752 will be provided to the LCPW through the US EPA and only 80 percent of the requested cost ($1,199,752) will be funded. LCPW is also seeking an emergency appropriation for the remaining 20 percent ($240,000) from fund reserves. There is sufficient fund balance to handle this project that was on the Public Works capital plan.
* The grant term is from September 2, 2024, to October 30, 2027, and was secured through the office of Congressman Brad Schneider.

..Body
RESOLUTION

WHEREAS, the Lake County Department of Public Works (LCPW) has received a grant from Congressionally Directed Spending through the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) Community Grants Projects; and

WHEREAS, these dollars will help to support construction funding for the replacement of the existing belt filter presses and associated equipment with new centrifuge technology at the LCPW New Century Town Water Reclamation Facility in Vernon Hills; and

WHEREAS, this grant amount totaling $959,752 has been awarded by the US EPA at 80 percent of the requested total project cost ($1,199,752); and

WHEREAS, the LCPW enterprise funds will be used to support the remaining 20 percent of the requested cost, and has sufficient funding to emergency appropriate these funds from Fund 610 Public Works Fund reserves; and

WHEREAS, the grant term is from September 2, 2024, to October 30, 2027.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by this County Board of Lake County, Illinois, that the amount of $959,752 is hereby accepted and appropriated for the LCPW in both grant revenue and capital expense and the 20 percent cost sharing amount ($240,000) is also authorized as an emergency appropriation for this project, as indicated in the attachment.

DATED at Waukegan, Illinois, on May 13, 2025.

matters.title: Joint committee action approving Change Orders Number One, Two, Three, Four, and Five for the Highland Lake Water System Project (Phase-2 New Water Supply Well Drilling and Testing) with Municipal Well and Pump resulting in a cost increase from $520,059 to $691,292.
matters.text:
..Title
Joint committee action approving Change Orders Number One, Two, Three, Four, and Five for the Highland Lake Water System Project (Phase-2 New Water Supply Well Drilling and Testing) with Municipal Well and Pump resulting in a cost increase from $520,059 to $691,292.

..Staff Summary
* Using awarded ARPA funds, on November 25, 2024, a contract was issued to Municipal Well and Pump to drill and test a new well on Lakeside Drive that will serve the Highland Lake Water System.
* Existing well log data provided a high level of confidence that sufficient water production would be found in the limestone formation aquifer, within 300 feet of the surface; sufficient production was not found within 300 feet of the surface, and the most prudent course of action is to drill additional well depth to the sandstone aquifer.
* Change Orders #1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 direct the contractor to continue well drilling, install casing pipe, compensate the contractor for unexpected downtime, modify the path of pumped test water, as well as descope unnecessary project elements, which resulted in a net increased cost of $171,233 (contract $520,059 to the final contract $691,292).
* The original contract received ARPA funds, and the contract was executed by the County Administrator; the additional funds ($171,233) necessary will be provided by the Department of Public Works enterprise funds and an emergency appropriation is requested.
* In accordance with Section 33.082 of the Lake County Purchasing Ordinance, when the total of change orders, contract modifications, or price adjustments on any contract approved by resolution by the County Board exceeds 10 percent of the original contract amount, approval of the standing committee in charge of the contracting department or agency and the Financial and Administrative Committee is required.
* This joint committee action authorizes and directs the Purchasing Agent to execute contract change orders one through five with Municipal Well and Pump increasing the original contract value from $520,059 to $691,292.

..Body
TO: 	Chair, Public Works & Transportation Committee 
      Chair, Financial & Administrative Committee
FROM: Yvette M. Albarran, Purchasing Agent
DATE: June 25, 2025
RE: Committee action approving Change Orders One through Five to the agreement with Municipal Well and Pump

Using awarded ARPA funds, on November 25, 2024, a contract was issued to Municipal Well and Pump to drill and test a new well on Lakeside Drive that will serve the Highland Lake Water System. Existing well log data provided a high level of confidence that sufficient water production would be found in the limestone formation aquifer, within 300 feet of the surface; sufficient production was not found within 300 feet of the surface, and the most prudent course of action is to drill additional well depth to the sandstone aquifer.

1. Change Order #1 directs the contractor to drill the well deeper into the sandstone formation until a better water production was estimated, resulting in an increased cost of $84,972.
2. Change Order #2 directs the contractor to install a 6" casing pipe through the limestone formation up to the sandstone layer, resulting in an increased cost of $193,532. Installing the 6" casing pipe is required for the well in accordance with IEPA requirements.
3. Change Order #3 is to compensate the contractor's downtime caused by the decision-making process for drilling deeper described in Change Order #1, resulting in an increased cost of $46,290.
4. Change Order #4 is to remove scope from the original contract and the Owner's Directed Allowance, resulting in a decreased cost of $165,341.
5. Change Order #5 directs the contractor to modify the path of pumped test water, resulting in an increased cost of $11,780.
6. Change orders #1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 result in a net increased cost of $171,233 from the original contract $520,059 to the final contract $691,292.
7. The original contract received ARPA funds, and the contract was executed by the County Administrator. The additional funds necessary will be provided by Department of Public Works enterprise funds.
8. In accordance with Section 33.082 of the Lake County Purchasing Ordinance, when the total of change orders, contract modifications, or price adjustments on any contract approved by resolution by the County Board exceeds 10 percent of the original contract amount, approval of the standing committee in charge of the contracting department or agency and the Financial and Administrative Committee is required.
9. This joint committee action authorizes and directs the Purchasing Agent to execute contract change orders #1 thru #5 with Municipal Well and Pump increasing the original contract value by $171,233 from $520,059 to $691,292.

matters.title: Joint resolution authorizing execution of a contract with Bolder Contractors, Inc., of Cary, Illinois, in the amount of $7,020,250 for the Vernon Hills West Pump Station Force Main Replacement Project and an emergency appropriation of $7,020,250 of Public Works reserve funds.
matters.text:
..Title
Joint resolution authorizing execution of a contract with Bolder Contractors, Inc., of Cary, Illinois, in the amount of $7,020,250 for the Vernon Hills West Pump Station Force Main Replacement Project and an emergency appropriation of $7,020,250 of Public Works reserve funds.

..Staff Summary
* The Lake County Department of Public Works owns and operates the Vernon Hills West Pump Station, which provides sanitary sewer service to portions of the Village of Vernon Hills and surrounding areas.
* The pump station conveys wastewater to the New Century Town Water Reclamation Facility via two 16-inch diameter force main pipes that have reached the end of their service life, and to meet current and future sanitary sewer capacity needs, these force main pipes require replacement with new 16-inch and 20-inch diameter pipes.
* An invitation to bid was issued and sealed bids were received from three contractors for this work ranging from $7,020,250 to $10,280,450 for the Vernon Hills West Pump Station Force Main Replacement Project.
* The award of this contract is recommended to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, Bolder Contractors, Inc. of Cary, Illinois, in the amount of $7,020,250.
* This resolution authorizes and directs the County Purchasing Agent to execute a contract with Bolder Contractors, Inc. in the amount of $7,020,250.

..Body
RESOLUTION

WHEREAS, the Lake County Department of Public Works owns and operates the Vernon Hills West Pump Station, which provides sanitary sewer service to portions of the Village of Vernon Hills and surrounding areas; and

WHEREAS, the pump station conveys wastewater to the New Century Town Water Reclamation Facility via two 16-inch diameter force main pipes that have reached the end of their service life and need to be replaced; and

WHEREAS, these force main pipes are proposed to be replaced with new 16-inch and 20-inch force main pipes to meet current and future sanitary sewer capacity needs; and

WHEREAS, in accordance with the Lake County Purchasing Ordinance, bids were called for by publication for the Vernon Hills West Pump Station Force Main Replacement Project; and

WHEREAS, Bolder Contractors, Inc. is the lowest responsive, responsible bidder in the amount of $7,020,250.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by this County Board of Lake County, Illinois, that $7,020,250 of Public Works Enterprise reserve funds is hereby appropriated and the Purchasing Agent is hereby authorized and directed to execute a contract with Bolder Contractors, Inc., of Cary, Illinois, in the amount of $7,020,250 for the Vernon Hills West Pump Station Force Main Replacement Project; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that an emergency appropriation from the Public Works Reserve Fund to the Public Works Water/Wastewater Facility Construction capital account for the Vernon Hills West Pump Station Force Main Replacement Project as detailed on the attached financial spreadsheet is approved.

DATED at Waukegan, Illinois, on August 12, 2025.

Connelly Inc., dba Connelly Electric Co., of Addison, Illinois in the amount of $111,000 for the Petite Lake Road Pump Station Electrical Upgrade Project.

matters.title: Joint resolution authorizing execution of a contract with Copenhaver Construction, Inc., of Union, Illinois, in the amount of $230,751 for the Manitou Creek Shoreline Stabilization project at the East Main Pump Station.
matters.text:
..Title
Joint resolution authorizing execution of a contract with Copenhaver Construction, Inc., of Union, Illinois, in the amount of $230,751 for the Manitou Creek Shoreline Stabilization project at the East Main Pump Station.

..Staff Summary
* The Lake County Department of Public Works owns and operates the East Main Street Pump Station, which provides sanitary sewer service to residents and businesses within portions of the Villages of Hainesville, Round Lake, Round Lake Beach, Round Lake Heights, and Round Lake Park.
* Along the facility's east streambank, where Manitou Creek flows into Long Lake, erosion has become a significant problem, and without intervention, erosion threatens the stream corridor, the facility's access driveway, and the building itself.
* To halt further degradation and align with Lake County's Manitou Creek Watershed Plan objectives, improvements will be made to include a combination of gabion baskets, stone slope protection, and native vegetation.
* Funding for this project is supported by the Public Works FY26 Capital Improvement Program and also in part by the Lake County Stormwater Management Commission through a $10,200 Watershed Management Board Grant.
* The County received bids from eight (8) contractors for this work ranging from $230,751 to $805,981.90 for the Manitou Creek Shoreline Stabilization project.
* The award of this contract is recommended to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, Copenhaver Construction, Inc. of Union, Illinois in the amount of $230,751.
* This resolution authorizes and directs the County Purchasing Agent to execute a contract with Copenhaver Construction, Inc., in the amount of $230,751.

..Body
RESOLUTION

WHEREAS, the Lake County Department of Public Works owns and operates the East Main Street Pump Station, which provides sanitary sewer service to residents and businesses within portions of the Villages of Hainesville, Round Lake, Round Lake Beach, Round Lake Heights, and Round Lake Park; and

WHEREAS, along the facility's east streambank, where Manitou Creek flows into Long Lake, erosion has become a significant problem; and

WHEREAS, to halt further degradation and align with Lake County's Manitou Creek Watershed Plan objectives, improvements will be made to include a combination of gabion baskets, stone slope protection, and native vegetation; and

WHEREAS, in accordance with the Lake County Purchasing Ordinance, bids were called for by publication of the Manitou Creek Shoreline Stabilization project at the East Main Pump Station; and Copenhaver Construction, Inc. is the lowest responsive, responsible bidder in the amount of $230,751; and

WHEREAS, the project is budgeted in the Public Works FY26 Capital Improvement Program and will also be supported by a $10,200 grant from the Lake County Stormwater Management Commission.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by this County Board of Lake County, Illinois, that the Purchasing Agent is hereby authorized and directed to execute a contract with Copenhaver Construction, Inc., Union, Illinois in the amount of $230,751 for the Manitou Creek Shoreline Stabilization project at the East Main Pump Station.

DATED at Waukegan, Illinois on August 11, 2026.
